headline: Revenue up 161% to $14.6B, first profit as a listed company
summary: SpaceX revenue rose 161% to $14.6B and net income was $4.4B, against a $1.1B loss a year earlier, as AI revenue reached $7.6B. Up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become free to sell at the start of Thursday 22 October 2026, two trading days after these results.
points: AI became the largest segment: revenue rose 830% to $7.56B on new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition (completed 14 August, adding $608M of revenue) and wider Grok adoption.
Starlink consumer subscribers rose by 1.6 million in the quarter to 13.6 million, and monthly ARPU rose 5% from Q2 to $69, though it was $83 a year earlier.
Starship Flight 14, its first orbital flight and first revenue-generating mission, delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites, about 10 times the downlink capacity added by a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.
Of the $19.6B capital spending, $16.4B went to the AI segment as the COLOSSUS II compute buildout continued; SpaceX also agreed on 8 October to buy 800 MHz spectrum licences for Starlink Mobile.
On the results call, according to Reuters and CNBC, SpaceX said Tesla and SpaceX had formed special board committees to discuss a possible merger.
guidance: The results release gave no numerical outlook. On the call, according to Reuters, the finance chief said SpaceX expects fourth-quarter capital spending of $35B to $40B and reiterated an annual recurring revenue target of about $100B by the end of 2026. CNBC reported first-quarter 2027 revenue guidance of $33B to $37B, against an analyst average of $22.2B (LSEG).
reaction: SPCX traded at about $147.50 on 20 October before the results, according to CNBC. Shares were up 4.9% in extended trading after the call, according to Reuters at 18:25 ET (23:25 UK time); CNBC reported a gain of about 5%. Revenue of $14.58B beat the $12.72B analyst average and adjusted EPS of 45 cents beat 13 cents (LSEG, via CNBC).
